quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the vehicle ahead too closely.
Someone is sitting in a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your lane. If a driver in the next lane is too close to the car ahead, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. Use your horn when you pass a parked car with someone inside, or a pedestrian or cyclist in the street.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to stay safe riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead—their headlights help light the road, and their taillights bounce up and down on bumpy roads.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to do either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Uses some rear brake when you use the front brake.
Uses some front brake when you use the rear brake.
Uses equal braking on both front and rear brakes when either one is used.
Remembers your braking habits over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Uses some front brake when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking automatically when you use the rear brake. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your braking system.

questions.question: Why should you use both brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using one brake causes uneven wear.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes in normal stops helps you develop a habit. This habit is important in emergencies when using both brakes may save your life.

questions.question: To stop quickly, it is best to:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together to stop quickly.

questions.question: You may need less space between you and the vehicle ahead if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
The weather and traffic are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather and traffic are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions: slippery pavement, when you can't see through the vehicle ahead, or heavy traffic. You can use normal distance in perfect weather and traffic.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Motorcycle windshields:

options.text: Do not protect your eyes from wind.
Protect you from objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Which option gives a rider the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection as a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, how should you position it?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb
At the left edge of the parking space so other drivers can see it better

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist wear for good protection?

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed
Shoes that stop below the ankle

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves to protect your hands and improve your grip on the controls. Wear a full jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles. Boots should have low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs or rough surfaces.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
Either the right or center portions of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: When securing a load on a motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Place secured loads as low as possible. Placing them too high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects its balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides of the motorcycle to avoid pulling it to one side.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: Apply pressure to the handgrip on the side you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chances of crashing?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight
Use your turn signals and brake light to show your intentions
Search for hazards in your path

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers, communicate your intentions, and maintain space around you. Search for and identify hazards. Be prepared to react to anything. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is one thing a proper lane position will NOT help you do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger never do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see better and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. It makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Get on before the engine starts.
Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on only after the engine starts and is in neutral. Sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider:
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left. This is a hand signal used instead of mechanical turn signals.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal, as that may distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass only when safe, then signal and return to your lane.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest and is operated with your left foot.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire going flat. Instead, you will notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: The best sitting position when riding:

options.text: Requires your arms to hold you up.
Lets you easily reach all the controls.
Keeps your arms straight when holding the handgrips.
Keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you easily reach all the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot, and the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the safest way is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to approach at a right angle can be dangerous because it may send you into another lane.

questions.question: The faster you drink:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes the alcohol.
The less the alcohol will affect you.
The less likely you will get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Motorcyclists riding in a group should avoid riding in pairs because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections can make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to move around.
Riders on the left side cannot exit the highway easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to move around.
questions.explanation: When traveling in a group, motorcyclists should not ride in pairs. Each rider needs enough room to avoid hazards.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: Another car is following too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another car is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if another car is too close behind you. The other driver may not see the hazard that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light if you are about to slow down where other drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes to see if any traffic is nearby.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular driving routine.
Does not help because you cannot do anything about traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular driving routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular driving routine. Always check your mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have a front brake and a rear brake.
Have three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury while riding, you should wear all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move to the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only make it more dangerous by encouraging them to follow at a higher speed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble because this will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually releasing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not apply the brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: You should maintain a minimum following distance of _____ seconds.
questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase this to at least three seconds when riding in less than ideal conditions.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who have taken a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders who lack training and do not know their motorcycle well are most likely to crash.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Not on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: A passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. These signs tell drivers about traffic rules they must follow.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, sunglasses, and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What should a proper lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid hazards, and escape danger. It does not help you avoid traffic signals, which you must always obey.

questions.question: If a tire is flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Use the brake on the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: How do you brake hardest in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel for the hardest straight-line braking.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the road is wet or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead. Also increase it in heavy traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Keep riding, it will fix itself.
Slow down by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible to find and fix the problem.

questions.question: When are successful motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When other drivers can see them.
When they are faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the side of the road.
When they are on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When other drivers can see them.
questions.explanation: Successful motorcyclists are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and lane position to be more visible.
